questions.text: What surprised Amir most about moving to university?
opts: Non-academic challenges: washing machines, landlords, managing alone
questions.correct: Non-academic challenges: washing machines, landlords, managing alone
questions.hint: "I couldn't read the washing machine instructions. I didn't know how to argue politely with a landlord."

questions.text: How did Amir's English improve to fluency?
opts: Through necessity in real situations — fixing bugs, reading documentation
questions.correct: Through necessity in real situations — fixing bugs, reading documentation
questions.hint: "I was trying to fix a bug or understand an error message. The language was just the tool."

questions.text: According to the second text, what do university employers value most?
questions.hint: "Communication skills, critical thinking, adaptability, and the ability to work in teams."

questions.text: The second text says subject knowledge is not important at all.
questions.hint: "This does not mean that subject knowledge is unimportant." — it's necessary, just not sufficient.

questions.text: Both languages are ___ , but together they're enough. (Amir)
questions.hint: "Both languages are INCOMPLETE. But together they're enough." — final sentence of Reading 1.

questions.text: Daniyar in the dialogue says university has made him more ___.
opts: uncertain — and that feels like progress
questions.correct: uncertain — and that feels like progress
questions.hint: "University has made me more uncertain. And somehow that feels like progress." ✅

questions.text: What does Amir mean by "the language has become part of how you think"?
opts: He thinks directly in English without translating
questions.correct: He thinks directly in English without translating
questions.hint: "I noticed I had been writing... without once thinking about what the Kazakh would have been."

questions.text: What has Zhibek been doing since February?
opts: Doing data analytics for the volleyball team
questions.correct: Doing data analytics for the volleyball team
questions.hint: "I've been doing data analysis for the volleyball team since February."

questions.text: What has Rustam been secretly doing for himself?
questions.hint: "I've been writing. Essays, mainly. Not for university — just for myself."

questions.text: What is Baglan's main argument in the debate?
opts: University costs have risen while value hasn't kept pace with job market
questions.correct: University costs have risen while value hasn't kept pace with job market
questions.hint: "The cost has been rising... students are finding credentials don't guarantee employment."

questions.text: What does Aliya say online learning has NOT replicated?
questions.hint: "University has been providing something that no online course has replicated: sustained intellectual community."

questions.text: Aliya argues universities should be abandoned in favour of better online alternatives.
questions.hint: "The solution isn't to abandon university — it's to fund it better." ✅

questions.text: Kamila says doing something without being ___ to is usually what matters.
questions.hint: "Something you've been doing without being TOLD to. That's usually the thing that matters." ✅

questions.text: "She was studying when he called." — "was studying" is Past Continuous because:
opts: It was an ongoing background action interrupted by "called"
questions.correct: It was an ongoing background action interrupted by "called"
questions.hint: Past Continuous = ongoing background interrupted by Past Simple. ✅

questions.text: "When I arrived, she had already left." — "had left" is Past Perfect because:
opts: Her leaving happened BEFORE my arrival
questions.correct: Her leaving happened BEFORE my arrival
questions.hint: Past Perfect = the earlier of two past events. She left FIRST, then I arrived. ✅

questions.text: "She ___ (study) for three hours when he arrived." (duration before past moment)
questions.hint: Duration before a past moment = Past Perfect Continuous. "She HAD BEEN STUDYING for three hours when he arrived." ✅

questions.text: "She has been writing essays for two years." — This uses PPC because:
opts: The process/duration up to now matters
She will write for two more years
questions.correct: The process/duration up to now matters
questions.hint: PPC = ongoing process/duration from past to now. ✅

questions.text: "She has written 5 essays this semester." — Why PPS not PPC?
opts: Counting completions requires PPS — PPC cannot count
questions.correct: Counting completions requires PPS — PPC cannot count
questions.hint: Counting → always PPS. "has WRITTEN 5 essays." NOT "has been writing 5 essays." ✅

questions.text: "I ___ (know) her for ten years." — Correct form:
questions.hint: "know" = stative verb → PPS only. "I HAVE KNOWN her for ten years." ✅

questions.text: "I'll get the door." — "will" here expresses:
questions.hint: "will" for spontaneous decisions/offers at the moment of speaking. ✅

questions.text: "The conference starts at 9 a.m." — Present Simple for future because:
questions.hint: Present Simple = fixed schedules/timetables. ✅

questions.text: "Look at those clouds — it ___ (rain)!" (evidence-based prediction)
questions.hint: Visible evidence → prediction = GOING TO. "It IS GOING TO RAIN!" ✅

questions.text: "He adapted to English through necessity." "Adapted" means:
opts: Changed to suit a new situation
questions.correct: Changed to suit a new situation
questions.hint: "adapt" = to change and adjust to suit a new situation.

questions.text: "Subject knowledge is necessary, not sufficient." "Sufficient" means:
questions.hint: "sufficient" = enough for the purpose; adequate. "Not sufficient" = not enough on its own.

questions.text: "She simultaneously managed three tasks." "Simultaneously" means:
questions.hint: "simultaneously" = at the same time as other things.
